issues.legal_issue: Acquisition under a supplementary scheme that advances a public town-expansion and industrial-development scheme is for an authorized public purpose even when land is allotted to a private industrial concern for development.
material_facts: The original scheme sought industrial development and relief of congestion by encouraging movement from crowded areas.
The supplementary scheme acquired additional land because the area provided under the original scheme was inadequate for the industrial concern's requirements.
The Trust retained general supervision and control, and the concern was to develop the land subject to town-planning controls.
issues.conclusion: The original and supplementary schemes were one composite scheme serving industrial development and relief of congestion; the acquisition was not a device to secure private gain and was for the purposes of the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 24(h) and 32 of the United Provinces Town Improvement Act, 1908, permit a town-expansion scheme that provides for industrial development and residence for employees and others. A supplementary scheme that effectuates the public purpose of the original scheme is not invalid merely because land is to be allotted to a private concern for development under the Trust's control. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

rule.if: challenge_to_acquisition_scheme and supplementary_scheme_advances_original_public_plan and trust_retains_development_control and not acquisition solely_for_private_gain

predicates.challenge_to_acquisition_scheme: The proceeding challenged the validity of an acquisition made under a supplementary scheme.
predicates.supplementary_scheme_advances_original_p: The supplementary scheme provided additional land to further the public objectives of an existing development scheme.
predicates.trust_retains_development_control: The public body retained general supervision and control over development of the land.
predicates.acquisition solely_for_private_gain: The land was acquired solely to transfer it to a private concern for that concern's private gain.
predicates.acquisition_serves_authorized_public_pur: The acquisition serves an authorized public purpose.

issues.definition: When a challenged supplementary scheme advances an existing public plan under the public body's continuing control and is not solely for private gain, the acquisition serves an authorized public purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A town-expansion scheme may use compulsory acquisition powers for land necessary to execute the scheme even though the provision describing that type of scheme does not itself expressly state the acquisition power.
material_facts: The Trust framed and sanctioned a town-expansion scheme and acquired land needed to carry it out.
The appellants challenged the Trust's power to acquire land compulsorily under that type of scheme.
issues.conclusion: The Trust had power to acquire the land compulsorily for executing the supplementary scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(a) authorizes acquisition of property necessary for or affected by execution of a scheme and applies to the improvement-scheme types described in section 24. Sections 32, 55 and 56 also support acquisition for a town-expansion scheme; the absence of a separate express acquisition provision in section 32 does not exclude the general power. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition_powe: The proceeding challenged a public body's power to acquire land compulsorily for a scheme.
predicates.land_needed_to_execute_scheme: The land was necessary for or affected by execution of the scheme.
predicates.scheme_is_town_expansion: The scheme was a town-expansion scheme.
predicates.trust_may_compulsorily_acquire_land: The public body may compulsorily acquire the land to execute the scheme.

issues.definition: If a challenge concerns compulsory acquisition for a town-expansion scheme and the land is needed to execute it, the public body may compulsorily acquire the land.

issues.legal_issue: The special procedure for acquisition for a company need not be followed when land is acquired for a public development scheme and is later allotted to a company to develop under public control.
material_facts: The land was acquired to carry out the Trust's industrial-development and town-expansion scheme.
The land was to be allotted to the company for development under the Trust's general supervision and control.
The scheme included a provision for sale or allotment of land.
issues.conclusion: Part VII of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, did not have to be followed because the land was acquired for the Trust's scheme, not for the company; including provision for sale of scheme land did not invalidate the scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Part VII of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, must be followed when land is acquired for a company, but not when it is acquired for a public scheme and later allotted for development as part of that scheme. Sections 23(g) and 65 of the United Provinces Town Improvement Act, 1908, permit provision for sale or disposal of scheme land. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

rule.if: challenge_to_acquisition_procedure and land_acquired_for_public_scheme and not land_acquired_for_company

predicates.challenge_to_acquisition_procedure: The proceeding challenged the procedure used to acquire land under a public scheme.
predicates.land_acquired_for_public_scheme: The land was acquired to carry out a public development scheme.
predicates.land_acquired_for_company: The land was acquired for a company rather than for the public scheme.
predicates.company_acquisition_procedure_not_requir: The special procedure for acquisition for a company is not required.

issues.definition: When challenged land was acquired for a public scheme rather than for a company, the special procedure for acquisition for a company is not required.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition award cannot be challenged solely on the ground that a different acquisition route might have produced greater compensation when the acquisition under the applicable law was valid.
material_facts: The appellants challenged awards made in acquisition proceedings under the Town Improvement Act.
They argued that another acquisition route might have entitled them to additional compensation.
The acquisition under the Act was valid and the Trust had power to acquire the land.
issues.conclusion: The awards were not open to challenge on the ground that use of another acquisition route might have resulted in greater compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Where the applicable Act validly authorizes compulsory acquisition, an award under that Act is not invalid merely because another acquisition process might have yielded greater compensation. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.appeal_challenging_acquisition_award: The proceeding challenged an award made in compulsory-acquisition proceedings.
predicates.acquisition_authorized_under_applicable_: The law used for the acquisition validly authorized compulsory acquisition of the land.
predicates.complaint_only_that_another_route_might_: The challenge asserted only that a different acquisition route might have resulted in greater compensation.
predicates.award_not_invalid_on_alternative_compens: The award is not invalid on the ground that another acquisition route might have produced greater compensation.

issues.definition: If a validly authorized acquisition award is challenged only because another route might have produced greater compensation, the award is not invalid on that ground.
